Results.ReviewText:
Major issues with the gas regulator. The one supplied uses a cheap plastic retaining ring near the hose that if its put under any stress (even mild stress), it gives way and allows gas to escape out the side.  I obtained a replacement from Weber, which I thought was great at the time (maybe i was sold a faulty one), but after installing the replacement and placing the tank back on its hanger, i could hear gas escaping again anytime the hose was not situated perfectly strait where it connects to the gas tank.  Propane will escape just next to the black screw on connector that you use to tighten the regulator onto the propane tank.  This really seems like one of the places where you might not want to cut corners as having a gas leak in any circumstance could cause a fire / explosion.  

At this point it appears as though i will have to obtain a decent gas regulator from another source since the model supplied (made in China), leaks way to easily.  After a search online, I see others have complained about this same issue.  I can see a date on my replacement regulator (7/21) that may be its manufacture date.  

The grill works well for cooking, but can struggle to get to a suitable cooking temperature if the ambient outdoor temp falls below freezing, or has significant wind passing by.   Also if you attempt to move it, and lift it by the tray opposite the wheels to roll it, the tray can detach from the size of the grill, as its not sturdily secured with the hardware provided.  This grill can also blow over in the wind if you put a grill cover on it as the base is not heavy enough to hold it by itself (I now weight it down since that happend 1x and left a dent in the lid).
Results.Title: Supplied gas regulater leaks easily
